finance.result: core IFRS 16 and revised FRS 102 lease claims supported by current official material
verifiedClaims: IFRS 16 uses a single lessee model requiring recognition of a right-of-use asset and lease liability for ordinary leases with stated recognition exemptions.
IFRS 16 subsequent measurement includes liability interest/payment mechanics and specified remeasurement or modification requirements.
The FRC's Periodic Review 2024 has a principal effective date of 1 January 2026 for FRS 102 and substantially revised Section 20 Leases.

The FRC's June 2026 explainer says most lessee leases are recognised as right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, with short-term and low-value recognition exemptions and a wider low-value accommodation than IFRS 16 subject to FRS 102 conditions.

FRS 102 transition material provides a modified-retrospective route and, in specified circumstances, an option to use IFRS 16 carrying amounts prepared for inclusion in IFRS consolidated financial statements.
finance.publicationNote: Keep discount rates and contract facts as explicit fictional inputs; recheck the current FRS 102 edition and implementation material immediately before publication.

payroll.result: pay-base and pension distinctions supported by current Revenue guidance without embedding statutory rates
verifiedClaims: Revenue's current payroll-submission guidance distinguishes gross pay, pay for Income Tax, pay for USC and pay for employee PRSI.

Qualifying regular employee pension contributions may reduce pay for Income Tax under the applicable conditions, while Revenue states they are not deducted from gross pay for USC or PRSI calculations.
Revenue states USC is operated on gross pay before employee pension contributions are deducted.
Revenue's employee-PRSI pay guidance includes applicable gross/notional pay and keeps specified employee pension contributions chargeable for PRSI.
Employee pension deductions, employer pension contributions and employer PRSI are distinct payroll layers; scheme-specific conditions must still be checked.
payroll.publicationNote: Recheck Revenue immediately before publication because pension and payroll rules are date-sensitive. The lesson must continue to omit current PAYE, USC and PRSI rates.

english.result: data-summary, evidence and presentation-structure objectives supported by British Council material
verifiedClaims: British Council data-description guidance emphasises selecting key features, stating specific figures and units, and giving an overview rather than narrating every data point.
British Council trend materials distinguish the size/direction of changes and encourage precise comparison language.
British Council advanced report guidance links findings and statistics to evidence-based recommendations.
British Council presentation practice uses structure, signposting, summary and opening the discussion for questions.
